notes: Hiring a car is best (25-40 EUR per day). KTEL buses run regularly between Heraklion, Rethymno and Chania. Three nights in Chania and two in Heraklion is ideal (a two-base plan).

Summer temperatures reach 30-35°C. Samaria, the Balos boat and Elafonisi are in full season. Stay in the shade between 12:00 and 16:00. August is the busiest month, and the sea stays around 25°C until September.
Knossos costs 20 EUR (museum separate), Samaria 5 and Spinalonga 8. A taverna meal costs 15-25 EUR, raki is often offered free, and for tips you round up the bill.
Cretan cuisine: dakos, staka, kalitsounia (small cheese pastries), snails (chochlioi) and tsikoudia. Tap water is drinkable in Chania.
Driving the Balos dirt road voids rental car insurance, so take the boat or a jeep. After Samaria, the ferry and bus run late in the day.
In summer there are direct flights from Türkiye to Heraklion and Chania. A Schengen visa is required.

stops.name: Knossos Palace
stops.tips: The palace of Minos and the labyrinth legend. Arrive at the 08:00 opening, as midday is hot and tour groups arrive. Expect Evans's restorations, and book tickets online.

stops.name: Heraklion Archaeological Museum
stops.tips: Minoan frescoes (the Prince of the Lilies, the Bull-Leaping fresco) and the Phaistos Disc. Air-conditioned.

stops.name: Heraklion Venetian Harbour & Koules
stops.tips: A Venetian fortress and a walk along the breakwater.

stops.name: Peskesi Heraklion
stops.tips: Cretan cuisine: dakos (barley rusk with tomato and cheese), staka (cream-based dish), wild greens and farm produce.

stops.name: Lions Square & Morosini Fountain
stops.tips: The city centre. Try bougatsa (custard pastry) at Kirkor.

backups.name: Agios Minas Cathedral
backups.tips: The largest cathedral in Crete. An alternative to the harbour.

stops.name: Rethymno Venetian Harbour
stops.tips: On the way (1.5 hours by KTEL bus). Take in the Venetian lighthouse and narrow lanes.

stops.name: Fortezza Rethymno
stops.tips: A 16th-century fortress with views over the Aegean.

stops.name: Taverna Knossos Rethymno
stops.tips: A family taverna by the harbour. Order the grilled fish.

stops.name: Chania Venetian Harbour
stops.tips: 1 hour by bus. See the Egyptian lighthouse, the Mosque of the Janissaries and the Venetian shipyards (Neoria).

stops.name: Chania Old Town Topanas & Splantzia
stops.tips: The Turkish and Venetian quarters. Walk the leather street (Skridlof) and enjoy the evening lights.

backups.name: Tamam Chania
backups.tips: A restaurant in an old Turkish bathhouse serving Cretan-Ottoman food.

backups.name: Arkadi Monastery
backups.tips: The monastery of the 1866 resistance. A detour from Rethymno along a mountain road (by car).

stops.name: Kissamos Port Balos Boat
stops.tips: 40 minutes from Chania. Daily boat to Gramvousa island (May to October, about 30 EUR).

stops.name: Gramvousa Fortress
stops.tips: A Venetian fortress on the pirate island. A 137 m climb, plus a shipwreck.

stops.name: Balos Lagoon
stops.tips: Pink sand and a shallow turquoise lagoon with world-famous views. The boat waits 3 hours, and there is no shade.

stops.name: Kissamos Taverna Sunset
stops.tips: On the way back, stop at a seaside taverna in Kissamos for stifado (beef stew) and local wine.

backups.name: Falasarna Beach
backups.tips: An ancient harbour and a long beach, good for sunset. An alternative to Balos (by car).

backups.name: Cellar Tavern Kissamos
backups.tips: A family taverna in central Kissamos. Lunch option if you skip the boat.

stops.name: Samaria Gorge Xyloskalo Entrance
stops.tips: Take the 06:15 bus from Chania, 1 hour to Omalos. The descent is 16 km and takes 5 to 7 hours (open May to October). Bring water and trainers, and look out for kri-kri goats.

stops.name: Samaria Abandoned Village
stops.tips: An old village halfway along the trail. Rest and refill water.

stops.name: Iron Gates Sideroportes
stops.tips: The canyon narrows to 3 m. The tightest point.

stops.name: Agia Roumeli
stops.tips: The coastal village at the gorge exit. Swim and eat at a taverna, then take the 17:30 ferry to Sougia or Chora Sfakion, and a bus from there to Chania.

stops.name: Chora Sfakion Ferry Return
stops.tips: A ferry ride on the Libyan Sea, then a bus to Chania, arriving at 20:30.

backups.name: Imbros Gorge
backups.tips: An easy 8 km gorge. Choose it if Samaria is closed or too hard.

stops.name: Elafonisi Beach
stops.tips: 1.5 hours from Chania (bus at 09:00 or by car). A pink-sand shallow lagoon: walk out to the island and rent a sunshade. It gets crowded at midday.

stops.name: Elafonisi Taverna Innachorion
stops.tips: A taverna behind the beach. Try the Cretan salad.

stops.name: Chrysoskalitissa Monastery
stops.tips: A white monastery on a rock, with the legend of the golden step.

stops.name: Topolia Gorge & Agia Sofia Cave
stops.tips: A canyon and a cave church on the way back.

stops.name: Chania Dinner To Maridaki
stops.tips: Seafood meze in Chania's old town.

backups.name: Kedrodasos Beach
backups.tips: An empty cedar-lined beach next to Elafonisi. A 20-minute walk.

backups.name: Milia Mountain Retreat Restaurant
backups.tips: Organic food in a mountain village. A detour.

stops.name: Plaka Spinalonga Boat
stops.tips: The way back to Heraklion runs east (by car or KTEL). From Plaka the boat takes 5 minutes (20 minutes from Elounda).

stops.name: Spinalonga Island
stops.tips: A Venetian fortress and a leper colony from 1903 to 1957 (the setting of the novel The Island). The walk takes 1 hour.

stops.name: Elounda
stops.tips: A luxury bay village. Try octopus at a harbour taverna.

stops.name: Agios Nikolaos Voulismeni Lake
stops.tips: The legend of the bottomless lake. Cafes and the harbour.

stops.name: Ammoudara Beach Heraklion
stops.tips: A long beach near Heraklion, good for sunset.

backups.name: Kritsa & Panagia Kera
backups.tips: A mountain village and Byzantine frescoes. An alternative to Agios Nikolaos.

backups.name: Ferryman Taverna Elounda
backups.tips: Used as a location for The Island. On the shore.

stops.name: Heraklion Central Market 1866 Street
stops.tips: Honey, olive oil, raki (tsikoudia) and herbs. Good for souvenirs.

stops.name: Nikos Kazantzakis Tomb
stops.tips: The author of Zorba. His gravestone on the walls reads "I hope for nothing", and the view over the city is superb.

stops.name: Ippokampos Heraklion
stops.tips: A harbour meyhane (tavern). Squid and meze for a farewell meal.

stops.name: Heraklion Airport Bus
stops.tips: 15 minutes by bus or taxi. Farewell.

backups.name: Phyllosophies Heraklion
backups.tips: A cafe on the square. Try the pastries.
